statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail 11 is in the low band and well below the block threshold.
recommendation: The session-extreme holding observed an hour ago has resolved into an orderly retracement: NQ printed a new high at 29,678.00, then eased about 97 points and is holding mid-to-upper range while ES, SMH and VIX moved consistently with it. That completed retracement, alongside an advance that stays narrow outside technology, lowers the assessment within the low band. The mapped policy state is EA_ON. The single mapped danger window remains 14:00-15:30 UTC on Aug 28 around the Fed chair's Jackson Hole keynote and the final Michigan sentiment reading. Existing-position management, exits and emergency protection remain unchanged.
headline: NQ prints a new 29,678.00 session high, then retraces about 97 points and holds it; VIX firms off its 14.42 low and breadth stays narrow, so Tail eases to 11
body: Nasdaq-100 E-mini futures trade at 29,580.75, up 291.25 points or 0.99%, roughly five hours into the U.S. cash session. The session range is 29,401.75-29,678.00 against a 29,499.50 open. The decisive change since the prior assessment is the character of the move rather than its direction: an hour ago NQ had cleared the thrice-rejected 29,660 shelf and was holding within ten points of the high, which was scored as observed session-extreme holding. That structure has now resolved. A marginal new high at 29,678.00 was rejected, price has retraced about 97 points, and the pullback is holding. A completed retracement after a session extreme is the specific evidence that mean reversion is still functioning, and it is the reason the assessment steps down rather than up. Cross-asset confirmation is consistent and orderly. QQQ trades at 719.37, up 1.12%, off a 720.62 range high with the 714.53 session low untouched. E-mini S&P futures are at 7,732.50, up 0.55%, about 23 points below their 7,755.50 high. Semiconductors, the strongest sector of the day, show the same shape: SMH at 568.83, up 2.35%, roughly four dollars below its 572.77 high. Volatility firmed rather than collapsed: VIX is 14.63, down 0.58 or 3.81% on the day, but back off the 14.42 session low that was in place an hour ago, which is what an orderly fade from highs produces. Rates are not a pressure source. The 10-year yield is 4.68% and the 2-year 4.24%, each up two basis points or less, and the 10-year was quoted at 4.66% at the open, so the curve has barely moved through a 1% index advance. Breadth remains the clearest conflict in the picture. Reported index moves put the Nasdaq composite up roughly 1.4% against a Dow gain of about 0.3%, with Nvidia up close to 9% after its results and Salesforce sharply higher, while wire reporting during the afternoon noted more decliners than advancers within the S&P 500. That narrowness reduces directional conviction and raises Stress; under the standing evidence rules it does not by itself raise Tail. Energy is the one genuinely energetic cross-asset. WTI is at 83.70 dollars, up 1.79%, having covered 80.65 to 84.27 intraday, with Brent at 89.68 dollars, up 2.59%. Against the unresolved Middle East supply backdrop that keeps energy a live Stress and headline input, but with equities higher on the day there is no negative transmission to price. On the calendar, jobless claims printed this morning at 203,000 against a 210,000 consensus and the July PCE report is already behind the market. Ahead lies the single catalyst cluster of the horizon: Chicago PMI at 13:45 UTC and the Fed chair's first Jackson Hole keynote as chair together with the final Michigan sentiment reading at 14:00 UTC on Aug 28, which is what the mapped danger window covers. Nothing in the observed path supports persistent one-way structure now, so Tail settles at 11 in the low band while Stress at 47 carries the narrow breadth, the energy move and the pending keynote.

lookbackSummary: The window runs from 18:00 UTC on Aug 26 to 17:00 UTC on Aug 27 and covers the Nvidia release and its full digestion into a technology-led advance. The first two hours were mixed and calm at Tail 10-11 while Stress climbed to 60-61 as positioning built into the report. The 20:00 UTC release hour was the only non-green hour in the window, moving to WATCH at Tail 21 and Stress 66. Futures reopened at 22:00 UTC on the beat and raised guidance, and the assessment stepped down through 18, 16, 13 and 12 in event/whipsaw mode as the gap held without extending. From 03:00 UTC the regime returned to mixed at Tail 10-11 with Stress easing to 45-47 through the Asian and European hours, the calmest stretch of the window. The 13:00 UTC hour lifted to Tail 14 and Stress 54 into the cash open, then eased back through 12, 12 and 11 as the opening auction faded and the range absorbed flow rather than extending. The 17:00 UTC hour rose to Tail 14 in trend-up mode when NQ cleared the 29,660 shelf and held within ten points of a new session high. Three hours have no published Claude assessment and are marked unavailable: 21:00 UTC on Aug 26, and 00:00 and 09:00 UTC on Aug 27.
outlookSummary: The horizon runs from 18:00 UTC today to 17:00 UTC on Aug 28 and contains a fading U.S. afternoon, an empty overnight and one genuine catalyst cluster at the far edge. With the session-high break now retraced, conditional Tail holds at 11 for the current hour, lifts to 13 across the 19:00 UTC power hour for closing imbalances and early month-end flow, then eases to 12 into the cash close. The 21:00 UTC maintenance break is the structural low of the horizon at 9, and a 10-11 overnight floor holds through the Asian hours in normal mode, with the Jackson Hole programme release around 00:00 UTC the only scheduled item. From the 06:00 UTC European pre-open the path drifts up through 11-13 as the keynote countdown compresses positioning, reaching 14 in the U.S. pre-market and 16 in the 13:00 UTC hour that carries the Friday cash open alongside Chicago PMI. The only two hours outside the low band are conditional Tail 22 at 14:00 and 15:00 UTC, where the keynote and the final Michigan reading land together and where any delayed second leg would follow. The horizon closes at 17 and 15 on the assumption that post-event price discovery is orderly and retracements occur.
